title: Behavioral Economics
text: Behavioral economics combines insights from psychology and economics to understand how people actually make decisions, which often deviate from the rational agent model assumed in classical economics. Key concepts include loss aversion (losses are felt more strongly than equivalent gains), anchoring (over-reliance on first information encountered), hyperbolic discounting (preference for smaller immediate rewards over larger future ones), and status quo bias. Behavioral economists Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky developed prospect theory to describe actual decision-making under uncertainty. Richard Thaler and Cass Sunstein popularized the application of behavioral insights to policy through nudges — subtle changes in how choices are presented that guide people toward better outcomes.
